sections.extract: Standard model physics from an algebra? by C. Furey A thesis presented to the University of Waterloo in fulﬁllment of the thesis requirement for the degree of Doctor of Philosophy in Physics Waterloo, Ontario, Canada, 2015 c⃝C. Furey 2015 arXiv:1611.09182v1 [hep-th] 16 Nov 2016

sections.title: Abstract
sections.extract: This thesis constitutes a first attempt to derive aspects of standard model particle physics from little more than an algebra. Here, we argue that physical concepts such as particles, causality, and irreversible time may result from the algebra acting on itself. We then focus on a special case by considering the algebra $\RCHO$, the tensor product of the only four normed division algebras over the real numbers.

The model is named after its inventors, J. Pati and A. Salam, who published the proposal in 1974, [57]. The Pati-Salam model may be considered to be a more conservative approach to uni- ﬁcation. sections.extract: Introduction Despite the wide range of proposals to simplify the standard model, most schemes tend to share the same impedances.
